description: We are building "Echoes Beyond Earth", an interactive website telling the stories of equipment left behind on the Moon and Mars. Looking for passionate members in web development, design, and storytelling to join us!
summary:
ECHOES_BEYOND_EARTH is an interactive digital archive developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, addressing the challenge "Abandoned but not Forgotten: Storytelling about NASA's Discarded Equipment on the Moon and Mars."

Our project transforms forgotten space equipment into meaningful scientific stories. Through an interactive web experience, users can explore lunar and Martian environments, discover historical missions, and learn about the instruments, experiments, and equipment left behind during space exploration.

The platform combines 3D terrain exploration, mission storytelling, scientific information, visual resources, and interactive educational activities to make space history more accessible and engaging.

By highlighting the scientific purpose and historical significance of abandoned equipment, ECHOES_BEYOND_EARTH encourages people to look beyond the missions themselves and appreciate the technology and discoveries that continue to shape our understanding of the Moon and Mars.

Because even when a mission ends, its story doesn't have to.
details:
Project Overview

ECHOES_BEYOND_EARTH is an interactive educational web platform designed to document and explore the scientific legacy of human-made equipment left on the Moon and Mars.

How It Works

The platform provides an immersive exploration experience through interactive 3D lunar and Martian terrain. Users can navigate the environment, switch between celestial bodies, explore mission locations, and access information about selected equipment and experiments.

The website organizes scientific and historical content into mission stories, explaining the purpose of different instruments, their role in exploration, and their contribution to scientific knowledge. It also incorporates educational resources and interactive quizzes to encourage active learning.

Benefits and Intended Impact

The project makes space exploration history more accessible by transforming technical information into engaging visual stories. It raises awareness about the scientific and historical importance of abandoned equipment, encourages curiosity about planetary exploration, and provides an educational experience for students and space enthusiasts.

Technology and Development

The website was developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with WebGL and Three.js technologies for interactive 3D visualization. The development process involved designing the interface, implementing interactive elements, organizing scientific content, and integrating visual resources.

Creativity and Innovation

Instead of presenting abandoned equipment as isolated historical facts, the project connects each object to its original mission and scientific purpose. Its combination of 3D terrain exploration, interactive storytelling, and educational activities creates a more engaging way to discover the history of space exploration.

Design Considerations

The team considered scientific accuracy, accessibility, usability, visual clarity, and the importance of presenting reliable references. The platform was designed to make complex scientific information understandable while maintaining an immersive exploration experience.
